alt: The research log carries 10 of Component 4’s 85 marks, beside 75 for the report. It is a separate document, may be notes or prose, sits outside the 5000-word limit without extending it, records decisions rather than everything, and is monitored by the teacher through discussion.
caption: A separate, 10-mark document for decisions and reflection, not extra report words.

alt: Three linked activities in each entry: record what you found, reflect on what it means for your question, methods or argument, and plan what to do next and why. A log that only records dates and tasks is a diary; linking all three, with reflection at the heart, shows a researcher at work.
caption: An entry that only records is a diary; reflection turns it into evidence.

after: ## What to log at each stage
alt: Seven stages with what to log at each: topics considered and rejected; teacher feedback and your decision; sources evaluated as you go; method options and reasons; surprising or conflicting findings; drafting decisions and word-limit problems; and a final reflection on how your thinking and question changed.
caption: Every stage produces decisions worth a short, dated entry.

after: ## What to log at each stage
alt: Log entries trace a question’s development: three topics considered, a draft question on whether deep-sea mining is necessary for a low-carbon future, teacher feedback that “necessary” needs technical expertise, and a revised policy question on whether countries should permit deep-sea mining in international waters.
caption: Record the feedback and the decision, so the report can explain how the question developed.

after: ## What to log at each stage
alt: A model log entry split into three parts: it records two demand forecasts that disagree because of different battery assumptions, reflects that the economic case depends on a technology assumption, and decides to make that assumption a central point of comparison.
caption: A short entry can do all three jobs in three sentences.

after: ## How the log supports the report
alt: Dated log entries on feedback, decisions, methods, sources, findings and final reflection feed four parts of the report: the introduction on how the question developed, the methods section, the evaluation of how perspectives influenced the argument, and the conclusion.
caption: Go back to the log when you draft the introduction, methods and conclusion.
